extracted.intended_audience: Prospective applicants to the John Templeton Foundation 'Character Through Community' funding competition
extracted.subtask_short: Templeton Character Through Community grant application
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and selection standards for preparing and submitting an Online Funding Inquiry (OFI) and, if invited, a Full Proposal to the John Templeton Foundation's Character Through Community funding cycle. Covers eligibility, budget/duration rules, required materials, timelines, and review criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start the application with an Online Funding Inquiry (OFI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application process begins with an Online Funding Inquiry (OFI) submitted on the John Templeton Foundation’s application portal. In the Cycle & Area section of the application, select the 'Character Through Community' funding cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All OFIs must be submitted by June 11, 2021 for consideration. Applicants who are invited to submit a Full Proposal should expect to submit by October 15, 2021.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to the published timeline and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the Foundation's timeline: OFI submission (March–June 2021), review (June–July 2021), Full Proposal submission (August–October 2021) if invited, and notifications by specified dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OFIs due June 11, 2021. Applicants will receive OFI status by July 30, 2021. Full Proposals due by October 15, 2021 (if invited); Full Proposal status notifications by June 10, 2022. Proposed project start date must be no earlier than July 1, 2022 and no later than December 1, 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — organization must meet RFP criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone whose organization meets the criteria identified in the Character Through Community Request for Proposals is eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-U.S. organizations may apply. A wide range of organizations is welcome, though a significant majority of awardees are anticipated to have 501(c)(3) status or equivalent international nonprofit status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request amount should reflect cost and scope; consider ROI
rubrics_metrics.description: When determining your request amount, consider (a) the cost of your activities and (b) the scope of your impact. The request should accurately reflect fair market-rate costs for proposed activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: creating significant national change or a rigorous evaluation of a high-profile organization may require >$1,000,000 USD; local-level impact might be closer to $200,000 USD. Reviewers consider 'return on investment' as a key decision criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum and maximum request thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation generally does not plan to invite proposals requesting less than $50,000 USD or more than $3,000,000 USD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these thresholds when scoping your budget; requests outside this range are unlikely to be invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration limits by organizational status
rubrics_metrics.description: Project duration limits depend on organizational status: up to 36 months for organizations with 501(c)(3) nonprofit status, up to 33 months for all other organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not propose projects longer than the applicable maximum duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated project start date window
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposed projects should have an anticipated start date no earlier than July 1, 2022 and no later than December 1, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposed timelines align with this permitted start date range.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overhead / indirect costs policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation allows for an overhead/indirect cost component within the budget, which is no more than fifteen percent (15%) of the direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overhead/indirect cost should be included in the Total Request Amount. Lower percentages are welcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and lodging funding limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel and lodging for personnel employed by the Legal Organization can be completely underwritten by the Foundation for all project activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stricter limits apply for travel/lodging associated with those not employed by the Legal Organization (e.g., project co-leaders at other institutions or external presenters). Generally, Foundation does not fund projects with budgets that exceed 10% travel and lodging costs for persons not employed by the Legal Organization. The Foundation will not pay for first class or business travel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment and additional materials policy at OFI stage
rubrics_metrics.description: The online OFI fields are intentionally short; applicants should limit their entry to the OFI form and use the single attachment slot only if absolutely necessary for understanding the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send additional project information via email. The Foundation has found the space provided is sufficient for a succinct but detailed project description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of practice composition and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the community of practice team members that will help accomplish your goals in a cost-effective manner; members can come from the same organization or multiple organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider cost-effectiveness and ensure the community of practice represents a diversity of perspectives and experiences. The project team should be organized as a community of practice where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative submissions: single OFI per project and project leader
rubrics_metrics.description: If applying with collaborator(s) from another organization, only a single OFI should be submitted for the project. For the OFI, designate a single person as the Project Leader and include their organization's details in the Organization section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A project team or organization can submit multiple OFIs for different projects; if OFIs are on related projects or ideas, the Foundation encourages bundling them into a single initiative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations and references at OFI stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use judgment in deciding how many citations are necessary in the OFI. In-line citations for key references can be helpful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A full reference list is not expected at the OFI stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of feedback for declined OFIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to the large number of OFI submissions, the Foundation is unable to provide each applicant with specific feedback if their OFI is declined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect individualized critiques for declined OFIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and outputs should align with project goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes and Outputs will vary by project nature and should align with the stated goals (e.g., launching a curriculum vs. conducting an evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: For a new character-focused curriculum, outcomes should align with continued implementation; outputs could include curricula, trainings, meetings/conferences, and other resources. For an evaluation, outcomes should identify how answering research questions will impact understanding and practice; outputs could include academic papers, conference presentations, and updated practice materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant advice — specificity and unified focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful applications, especially those requesting more than $250,000 USD, should identify a specific opportunity or problem of practice that references a specific method to strengthen character programming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed activities with a unified focus are more often successful than proposals that are diffuse and lack an overarching narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria used by reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: External reviewers and internal Foundation staff will consider several criteria when reviewing OFIs: Alignment with Funding Competition objectives; Detailed project plan; Highly qualified and well-positioned project team; Anticipated impact; Cost effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should clearly state alignment with competition objectives, provide a detailed plan, demonstrate team qualifications and diversity (organized as a community of practice where appropriate), describe anticipated significance and outcomes/outputs, and justify cost effectiveness. All invited full proposals undergo both internal and external review and require approval by the JTF Board of Trustees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review process and board approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All invited full proposals will undergo both internal and external review, and all proposals require approval by the JTF Board of Trustees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for multiple review stages and the possibility of final board-level decisions affecting funding invitations.
